Leinweber Postdoctoral Fellow at the Leinweber Institute for Theoretical Physics at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor. My interests include quantum gravity, holography, multipartite entanglement, supergravity, and string theory.

## Academic appointments

### University of Michigan

[2024–present · Leinweber Postdoctoral Fellow]{.entry-meta}

Leinweber Institute for Theoretical Physics, Ann Arbor, Michigan. Research on supersymmetric black hole phases in AdS/CFT, the gravitational path integral, superconformal indices, and black hole decoherence.

### Tata Institute of Fundamental Research

[2019–2024 · Doctoral researcher]{.entry-meta}

Department of Theoretical Physics, Mumbai, India. Research on measures of multipartite entanglement and their holographic descriptions, including analytical and numerical calculations in Mathematica and Python. Other projects included supersymmetric black holes and non-local defects in conformal field theory.

### California Institute of Technology

[May–July 2017 · Summer research fellow, LIGO Laboratory]{.entry-meta}

Studied coating Brownian noise and developed a digital phase-locked loop on an FPGA for the experimental setup.

## Methods & tools

**Programming and scientific computing:** Mathematica, Python (NumPy, SciPy), C++, MATLAB, SageMath, Inkscape, LaTeX, Linux, and Git.

**Mathematical and numerical methods:** Linear algebra, differential equations, information theory, convex optimization, semidefinite programming, stochastic processes, and spectral analysis.

## Outreach & academic activities

- Organized two workshops on Quantum Black Holes at the Leinweber Institute for Theoretical Physics, University of Michigan.
- Volunteered at TIFR’s *Frontiers of Science* outreach events in 2019 and 2023.
- Volunteered for ICTS Bangalore’s Math Circle, Session 22, supporting mathematical problem solving for school students.
- Member of the IISER Thiruvananthapuram Astronomy Club (2014–2019), organizing stargazing sessions.
- Volunteered at *Anvesha*, the IISER Thiruvananthapuram science festival (2017).

## Earlier research

**Everyday Radio Telescope · IISER Thiruvananthapuram (2016).** Built a radio telescope with fellow students and worked on signal acquisition and spectral analysis. [Read the project paper](papers/1601.02982.qmd).
